$comment: ALERT RULES — declarative, operator-editable. No code change is needed to
adjust a threshold; edit this file and restart.
EVERY THRESHOLD HERE IS INFERRED. No specification supplied a single one.
Each rule therefore carries `rationale` (what the number is for) and
`confirmWith` (what a human must check before trusting it). `source` is
honest about that: INFERRED means nobody has confirmed it yet.
Read `config/alerts.schema.md` for the field-by-field meaning, and
`docs/alerting.md` for how absence is handled — in particular why a rule
can never report healthy because it received no data.
ABSENT_IS_ZERO    — a never-reported series counts as 0. Defensible only
ABSENT_IS_UNKNOWN — the rule cannot conclude, and says so. Never `ok`.

rules.title: Fuel-theft detector has produced no candidates
rules.description: Zero theft candidates while tanks are reporting means either no theft (good) or a broken detector (indistinguishable without this rule).
rules.rationale: This platform exists to catch fuel theft. A detector that stops reporting and a site with no theft look identical from the outside: both are zero. Silence is therefore treated as its own condition rather than as evidence of safety.
rules.confirmWith: Run the detector over a site with known historical loss and confirm it still produces candidates. Until that is done, treat this threshold as a starting point, not a tuned value.

rules.title: Tanks are reporting but the theft pipeline has never reported
rules.description: Ingest is alive (tank levels are moving) yet no theft candidate has EVER been produced. That is a broken pipeline, not a quiet site.
rules.rationale: Distinguishes a broken detector from a genuinely quiet one. Requires the ingest metric to be live, so it cannot fire during a total outage — during which the ingest rule is the one that speaks.
rules.confirmWith: Confirm the detector is actually invoked on the tick path and not merely exported and unused. Check `engine.ts` imports `detectUnexplainedLoss`.

rules.title: The simulation clock has not advanced
rules.description: No tick has run recently. Every derived figure on the dashboard is stale if this fires.
rules.rationale: The clock is driven by the server-side scheduler. A stopped scheduler is invisible on the dashboard — the last values simply stop changing, which reads as stability rather than failure. The comparison fires when the age is GREATER than the threshold, because a stalled clock is one that has not advanced recently.
rules.confirmWith: Confirm the expected tick interval for this deployment (see docs/telemetry-clock.md) and set a value comfortably above it. The shipped 10-minute threshold assumes the documented 5-minute interval plus headroom; it has NOT been confirmed against real traffic.

rules.title: The scheduler is not running at all
rules.description: The process-level scheduler handle reports not-running, so no tick will occur even when the conditions are otherwise normal.
rules.rationale: Complements the stall rule: a clock that has not run in a while and a scheduler that is not running are different faults with different fixes (a wedged tick versus a failed startup).
rules.confirmWith: Confirm the instrumentation hook that calls ensureScheduler() runs in this deployment profile and is not disabled by configuration.

rules.title: Interlock denials are spiking
rules.description: Many control commands are being refused by safety interlocks. Either a real unsafe condition, or a threshold set wrong.
rules.rationale: A rising denial count is the clearest signal that something on the fleet is unsafe, or that an inferred interlock threshold is wrong and is refusing safe operations. Both demand a human.
rules.confirmWith: This is a counter, so the threshold is a RATE not an absolute: confirm the observation window the preview reports, then set a number appropriate to fleet size. The shipped value of 0 means 'any denial is worth looking at'.

rules.title: Nobody is receiving pages
rules.description: Notification attempts are being made but no transport exists for them. Alerts and escalations are being produced into a void.
rules.rationale: Reuses the TransportOutcome vocabulary from notification-transport.ts rather than inventing an alerting-specific one. NO_TRANSPORT is deliberately distinct from FAILED: nothing was attempted, so an operator reading FAILED would go hunting a broken provider that does not exist.
rules.confirmWith: If this fires while NO_TRANSPORT is expected in an environment with no SMTP or SMS provider configured, mark it acknowledged rather than silencing the metric — the count is accurate.

rules.title: Notification sends are failing
rules.description: A transport exists and is refusing the sends. Distinct from having no transport at all.
rules.rationale: Paired with the NO_TRANSPORT rule so the two are separable at a glance. FAILED means something is misconfigured on a provider that exists; NO_TRANSPORT means no provider was ever configured.
rules.confirmWith: Check provider credentials and reachability. Do not treat this as the same problem as the NO_TRANSPORT rule.

rules.title: Database connection pool is saturated
rules.description: Most pooled connections are in use. Requests will queue or fail under this load.
rules.rationale: Saturation precedes connection errors rather than following them, so an alert on errors alone would fire only once requests were already failing.
rules.confirmWith: Confirm the pool size configured for this deployment (see connection_limit in DATABASE_URL) and the expected concurrent request count, then set a ratio appropriate to both.

rules.title: Database queries are erroring
rules.description: Query errors are being recorded rather than merely slow or saturated.
rules.rationale: A counter, so absence genuinely does mean zero errors and no information is lost by treating it as zero here.
rules.confirmWith: Check the structured logs for the error detail — this rule intentionally reports only the count, because the detail may contain tenant data.

rules.title: Rate limiter is degraded
rules.description: The limiter has fallen back to a weaker mode. Brute-force protection is reduced until it recovers.
rules.rationale: Degradation is an explicitly declared state rather than an inference, so it alerts on its own rather than as a side effect of some other metric moving.
rules.confirmWith: Confirm whether degraded mode is expected in this deployment (single-replica dev) or indicates the shared store is unreachable in production.

rules.title: Telemetry ingest is rejecting readings
rules.description: Device readings are being refused, so the platform's picture of the fleet is incomplete.
rules.rationale: Silent rejection is worse than a visible outage: the platform keeps answering queries while quietly holding stale data.
rules.confirmWith: Cross-check the rejection reason distribution in structured logs against device firmware versions in the field.
